answer: An onyx-hard identity anchor binds each agent to one device-bound key: one key can hold only one reputation, so cloning means buying a new device and a new bond each time. Reputation then grows like an orchard, slowly, only through verified work that peers spot-check, so a fresh fake starts barren and cannot harvest trust it never planted. Newcomers may water their sapling in a shared oasis of audited micro-tasks, earning small non-transferable credit that matures over several epochs; an attacker spinning up ten thousand clones pays ten thousand bonds and still waits epochs for that fruit.
